rationale: Adversarial re-scoping of the first recorded A2 finding. The finding's rationale implied that the missing sender-eligibility guard was peculiar to TimeoutNow among the consensus RPCs. Reading all five handlers in their admission order shows that is an overreach: requestVote and requestPreVote do decide eligibility, and they decide it before any term or authority effect, but appendEntries and installSnapshot also have no membership check and also adopt a higher term and record the sender as leader. The knowledge entry that supported the narrower reading is corrected rather than replaced, and a new question records the actual distribution; what remains specific to TimeoutNow is not the absence of a guard alone but that its authority effect (setting candidateFromLeadershipTransfer, which disables the known-leader rejection on the voting side) exists on no other path and carries no term to expire it.

investigations.question: Which consensus RPC handlers decide whether the sender is eligible, and where does that decision sit relative to the term and authority effects each handler performs?
investigations.hypothesis: All five handlers are admitted through one dispatch path whose only common check is checkRPCHeader (protocol-version bounds). Inside the handlers the behaviour splits: requestVote and requestPreVote return early when the sender's ID is absent from the latest configuration, and they do so before the term-adoption branch, so a sender outside the configuration cannot even raise the receiver's term; appendEntries and installSnapshot have no such check and will adopt a higher term and record the sender as leader (installSnapshot additionally installs the configuration carried in the request), and timeoutNow performs its transition with no check at all. So the eligibility guard is absent from three of the five handlers, not unique to TimeoutNow, and the transfer finding must rest on the transfer-specific effect rather than on uniqueness of the omission.
investigations.discriminator: Refuted if any of appendEntries, installSnapshot or timeoutNow consults the configuration (or another sender-authority condition) before its term/leader/transition effects, or if the vote handlers can adopt a term before rejecting an ineligible sender. A nonexistent-sender experiment would settle the non-member consequence, but the ordering question itself is decided by the handler bodies.
limitations: Source-only (this run's experiment capacity is exhausted); the distribution is read from handler bodies, and the non-member consequence assumes transport reachability, which the RPC layer deliberately does not provide on its own.

A member that is not the leader can perform the same term/leader effects by sending an AppendEntries/InstallSnapshot with a higher term, so the distribution matters mainly for the non-member or stale-sender case.

knowledge.statement: Sender eligibility is decided in only two of the five consensus handlers, and there it is decided before any authority effect. requestVote, after decoding the candidate, returns immediately when the candidate ID is absent from the latest configuration (and the check is skipped only when the configuration list is empty, the bootstrap case), then applies the known-leader rejection, the older-term check, the term-adoption branch that sets Follower and the new term, the non-voter rejection, and finally the vote rules; requestPreVote applies the same membership rejection before computing its answer. appendEntries and installSnapshot contain no membership or sender-authority check at all: both adopt a higher term and transition the receiver to Follower, both record the sender as the current leader from the request, and installSnapshot additionally replaces the receiver's latest and committed configurations with the request's contents. timeoutNow likewise checks nothing and performs its transition. The two vote handlers' guards are therefore real but local; the guarantee 'only eligible senders can be honoured' does not hold across the RPC surface.
knowledge.conditions: Read from the retained handler bodies in their admission order after checkRPCHeader (protocol-version bounds only, applied uniformly in processRPC). The vote handlers' membership check is bypassed when the receiver's latest configuration lists no servers, which the code documents as the bootstrap case.
knowledge.changed_premise: The earlier statement of this entry, by describing 'the sibling consensus RPC handlers' as applying an eligibility guard, invited the reading that the vote handlers' guard was a property of the RPC surface and hence that its absence on TimeoutNow was peculiar. The actual distribution is narrower: two of five handlers check sender eligibility, and the other three (appendEntries, installSnapshot, timeoutNow) do not, so the omission alone is not a distinguishing property of TimeoutNow. The earlier statement's description of the two vote handlers remains accurate; what changes is its scope, and consequently the earlier interpretation's claim that the eligibility guard is 'simply absent on the one path that can trigger an election and set the vote-bypass flag' is narrowed to what the transfer path uniquely does rather than to the uniqueness of an omission.

interpretations.rationale: The question is answered by reading where each handler decides eligibility relative to what it does with the message. Uniform admission exists: processRPC validates the header's protocol version and dispatches (raft.go:1390-1412), and checkRPCHeader is the only check applied to every command, so it cannot express sender eligibility. The vote handlers then do decide: requestVote rejects a candidate whose ID is absent from the latest configuration before the known-leader check and before the branch that adopts a higher term and sets Follower (raft.go:1636-1672), and requestPreVote rejects in the same place, which is why an ineligible sender is inert in those two paths. The log-transfer handlers do not decide: appendEntries goes from the older-term check straight to adopting a higher term, setting Follower and recording the sender as leader (raft.go:1440-1474), and installSnapshot does the same and further installs the configuration carried in the request (raft.go:1842-1852). timeoutNow performs the transition unconditionally (recorded behaviour, revision 1 of the TimeoutNow entry). Consequences for the recorded findings: the first finding's overreach is removed - the absence of a membership check is not peculiar to TimeoutNow, and under the standard transport-trust assumption a member could obtain comparable effects by sending a higher-term AppendEntries. What survives, and is specific to the transfer path, is (i) the effect: only TimeoutNow sets candidateFromLeadershipTransfer, and that flag is what makes the induced RequestVote winnable despite a known leader (recorded grant-path behaviour), and (ii) the missing context: TimeoutNowRequest carries no term, so a transfer request that outlives the sender's leadership cannot be detected, which does not require a non-member sender at all. The second finding's contract argument (explicit non-voter target) and the snapshot finding are untouched by this re-scoping, since neither depends on the uniqueness of the omission.

knowledge.assertion: Corrected scope: two of five handlers decide eligibility before their effects; the omission is not unique to TimeoutNow.
The transfer mark is produced only by timeoutNow and lives for one candidacy, which is what keeps the first finding transfer-specific.

counterevidence: The vote handlers' guards are genuine protective mechanisms for their paths: an ineligible sender cannot raise the receiver's term through a vote request, which is stronger than merely being refused a vote.

The transport-trust assumption is not part of this finding: Raft's RPC layer is unauthenticated by design, so the log-transfer omissions are benign whenever only members can reach the transport and members are not Byzantine.

The bootstrap carve-out (an empty configuration list grants) means the vote handlers themselves do not apply eligibility universally, which further weakens any claim that eligibility is a global RPC property.
limitations: No execution or receipt: the distribution is read from source, and no forged-sender round trip was observed (this run's experiment capacity is exhausted).
This record corrects the scope of an earlier assertion; the earlier revision remains available, and no other recorded finding was revised.
Whether an operator should treat a reached-but-ineligible sender as a defect depends on the deployment's transport protection, which the retained material does not describe.
interpretations.report_title: 修正与再界定：发送方资格检查只存在于两个投票处理函数中
interpretations.report_answer: 本次对第一条 A2 发现做了对抗性再界定（仅源码，实验额度已用尽）。事实是：五个共识 RPC 都经统一入口分派，而统一入口只校验协议版本；随后只有 requestVote 与 requestPreVote 会检查发送方是否在最新配置中，且在“采纳更高任期并转为 Follower”之前就返回，因此不合格发送方在投票路径上是惰性的；appendEntries 与 installSnapshot 都没有任何资格检查——它们会采纳更高任期、转为 Follower、把发送方记为该任期 leader（installSnapshot 还会用请求携带的配置替换本地配置）；timeoutNow 同样不做任何检查。因此“缺少资格检查”并非 TimeoutNow 独有，原知识条目的表述范围被修正（旧修订保留）。修正后仍然成立、且真正属于转移路径的两点：其一，只有 timeoutNow 会设置 candidateFromLeadershipTransfer，而该标志使被触发的 RequestVote 在投票者已知 leader 的情况下仍可胜选（已有授予路径记录）；其二，TimeoutNowRequest 不携带 term，因此“发送方已失去领导权”的过期转移请求无法被识别，而这一情形并不需要非成员即可发生。第二条（显式非投票目标）与快照循环发现不依赖“唯一遗漏”，故不受此次修正影响。
